protocol.question: Can a processor-budget upgrade invalidate only part of an existing collection, allowing exact replay for unchanged pages?
protocol.claim: Page-scoped input equivalence can recover safe reuse rejected by collection-wide processor invalidation, without admitting changed pages.
protocol.existing_gap: Existing component certificates require the entire collection output to match; one changed page prevents that certificate.
protocol.contract: Same pinned base processor implementation and all other settings. Budgets match the recorded v0.1/v0.2 change, but this isolates that change and does not certify all factory processor differences.
protocol.cpu_sample: The previously frozen independent-endpoint 200 pages, unchanged order and image hashes; no resizing or selection by outcome.
protocol.decision: Compare every processor output field, shape, dtype and byte payload per page; replay only when equal AND all remaining upstream dependencies are unchanged. A matching grid alone is insufficient.
baselines: Processor-config mismatch: raw for every page
Ignore processor change: replay every page
protocol.gpu_gate: Run only if CPU produces both equal and changed pages.
protocol.gpu_sample: First up to 8 equal and first up to 8 changed pages in frozen order, explicitly stratified diagnostic sample, not population estimate. Reuse original source states; independently encode target at 602112 pixels. Check both routed result and unsafe replay. At most 16 pages, one target adapter, no query benchmark.
measurements: Independent target versus routed representation bit equality
Unsafe replay mismatches on changed pages
protocol.cost_scope: Do not claim index speedup. Source output fingerprints are retrospectively computed for this diagnostic and must be recorded during initial encoding in deployment; report this extra CPU work separately.
protocol.failure_interpretation: If no mixed subset exists, do not broaden or tune the benchmark to manufacture one. If an admitted replay differs, reject the mechanism under this integration until dependencies or execution are understood. If all rejected outputs also match, the guard is conservative; do not claim rejection proves representation change.
